title: Cross-browser auth resilience, hardened actor init, responsive UI fixes, and smoke coverage

requirements.summary: Make the Internet Identity login flow resilient across major browsers with clear user-facing errors and guaranteed recovery from stuck states.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking “Login” (frontend/src/components/auth/LoginButton.tsx) initiates Internet Identity login successfully on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Opera/Opera GX in a clean session.
If login fails or the auth flow cannot be established, the UI shows a clear English error message to the user (not a silent failure) and the app remains usable.
The login button cannot remain indefinitely stuck in a “Logging in...” state; the UI must recover to an actionable state (e.g., allow retry) after an appropriate failure/timeout path.
No secrets or sensitive tokens are logged to the browser console as part of any new error handling.

file_operations.description: Harden the Internet Identity login implementation for cross-browser popup behavior and reliability: ensure the login attempt has a bounded timeout, errors are surfaced via loginError without logging sensitive data, and the state always transitions back to an actionable status on failure. Keep authentication semantics intact (stability/error-handling only).

Add resilient UI handling for login/logout: display clear English error feedback (e.g., toast/alert) when loginError occurs or when a timeout/failure happens, prevent indefinite “Logging in...” by offering retry, and avoid any console logging of sensitive values. Use the existing shadcn-ui Button and app toast system; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Create a small utility that maps common Internet Identity/AuthClient error cases (popup blocked, user cancelled, network/connection closed, already authenticated, initialization not ready) to clear, non-sensitive, English user-facing messages (no secrets/tokens included).

requirements.summary: Harden actor initialization so missing/blocked URL params or access-control initialization failures do not crash the app and logout remains stable across browsers.
acceptanceCriteria: The app loads and navigates normally in all target browsers even when URL parameters (e.g., the admin token parameter used by the actor initialization) are absent, blocked, or cleared.
If the actor access-control initialization fails for any reason, the failure is handled gracefully (no blank screen / unhandled promise rejection), and the user can still use non-admin public pages.
Logging out clears user session state without leaving the app in a broken state across target browsers.

file_operations.description: Make actor creation resilient: treat access-control initialization as best-effort (no crash if secret param is absent/empty), catch and handle initialization failures so the hook still returns a usable actor for public pages, and prevent unhandled promise rejections that differ across browsers. Avoid changing auth semantics beyond stability/error handling.

Reduce cross-browser fragility around secret/session parameter handling: avoid noisy console warnings, ensure sessionStorage failures do not break app flow, and ensure missing/cleared admin token results in a safe null/empty outcome without throwing.

Ensure admin gating remains robust when actor/admin-session checks fail (e.g., due to actor initialization variance across browsers): show a clear English fallback state and keep public navigation usable, without crashing or leaving a blank screen. Use the existing guard screens/components; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

On logout, ensure all user session UI state recovers reliably across browsers: clear admin verification progress and cached queries as currently done, and add any needed UI feedback for logout failures while keeping the app usable. Use the existing shadcn-ui Button; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Ensure the UI is responsive and functional across small phones, tablets, and desktop sizes, including header navigation, mobile menu, forms, and dialogs.
acceptanceCriteria: Header navigation (frontend/src/components/SiteHeader.tsx) remains usable on small screens: mobile menu opens/closes reliably, links are tappable, and content does not overflow horizontally.
All primary forms (Contact page, testimonial submission dialog, product checkout/quote path) remain readable and usable on mobile and tablet breakpoints without layout breakage.
All modals/dialogs used by the app remain accessible and scroll correctly on small screens (no content clipped off-screen with no way to reach it).
No page introduces horizontal scrolling at common viewport widths (e.g., 360px, 390px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px) except where explicitly intended for content.

file_operations.description: Improve small-screen navigation reliability: ensure the hamburger menu panel does not cause horizontal overflow, links remain comfortably tappable, and the menu closes predictably (including after navigation). Use existing shadcn-ui Button and current layout patterns; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Make the lightbox dialog mobile-safe: constrain dialog height, allow internal scrolling, ensure image/content stays within viewport on small screens, and avoid horizontal overflow. Use existing shadcn-ui Dialog components; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Ensure the testimonial submission dialog remains usable on small screens: responsive dialog width, scrollable content if needed, and button/layout spacing that works on phones. Use existing shadcn-ui Dialog/Input/Textarea/Button components; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Harden contact form responsiveness and usability on mobile/tablet: ensure inputs/select/textarea do not overflow, spacing remains readable, and the submit success message fits small viewports. Use existing shadcn-ui form components; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Validate responsive behavior of the product detail layout (image, badges, price, checkout/quote actions) across breakpoints, ensuring no horizontal scrolling and that the checkout/quote flow remains usable on mobile/tablet.

Add minimal global responsiveness safeguards (e.g., preventing unintended horizontal overflow and improving long-word wrapping where needed) using existing global styling entry points, without changing the overall theme.

requirements.summary: Add a lightweight cross-browser QA checklist and feasible automated smoke coverage for login and critical navigation to prevent regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: A documented QA checklist exists in-repo (English) specifying the minimum manual verification steps for Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Opera/Opera GX, including the Login flow and basic navigation.

At least one repeatable smoke test (or equivalent automated check supported by the current project setup) covers that the app renders, navigation works, and the login button does not hard-crash the UI when invoked.

file_operations.description: Document an English cross-browser QA checklist covering: clean-session login popup behavior (including popup-blocked scenario), logout recovery, basic navigation across main routes (Shop/Contact/Testimonials), and admin guard screens behavior. Include explicit target browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Opera/Opera GX.

Add a repeatable automated smoke test (using the project’s existing test tooling) that mounts the LoginButton with a mocked useInternetIdentity implementation and verifies clicking does not crash, the disabled state is respected, and an error path results in user-facing feedback without leaking sensitive data.

Add a minimal app render/navigation smoke test (using existing tooling) that mounts App within required providers and verifies key navigation renders without throwing, focusing on ensuring the login UI invocation does not hard-crash the UI.
Wire the smoke tests into an existing test script (or add a dedicated smoke script) consistent with the current React app tooling so the checks are easy to run locally and in CI.
